{"summary":"This packet contains only `lib/source-business-evidence.ts` and the project skill. The proposed Cycle25 rowspan helper, the unknown result `unknown_merged_price_options_unconfirmed`, the canonical bilingual explanation, the `sourceBusiness` checker branch and the delivery-assessment citation use are not in this source, so they cannot be reviewed as code defects. Reviewing the current code against what the design would need: the current table owner reads a table only from its third row downward, so it never inspects the first rows of a table. A two-row owner with no cell attributes is accepted in full and reduced to one cell-less price leaf. That leaf is read as a normal price-row claim: it drops the rowspan label, gives no row count and has no notion of merged rows. The price branch also requires the label to appear exactly once in body text, which a shared Tea label violates for two amounts. The result is the generic `unknown` reason `complex_or_unlocated_item`. That matches the reported current behaviour but contradicts the premise, and no recognized context exists to fill in. The explanation text describes only unlocated or duplicate content and does not ask the buyer which option applies. Two deterministic problems are also reachable in the current code: an uncontrolled exception on a malformed table, and an unbounded excerpt size in a covered citation witness. The design risks are listed separately as P3 and none of them is reported as an existing bug.","findings":[{"severity":"P2","file":"lib/source-business-evidence.ts","line":32,"title":"Any malformed table under budget throws instead of returning `unknown`","evidence":"`tablePriceLeaves` line 32 explicitly allows nested `\"table\"` tags inside `thead`/`tbody`/`tfoot` (`[\"table\",\"thead\",\"tbody\",\"tfoot\",\"tr\",\"td\",\"th\"].includes(tag) || tag === \"table\" && node !== owner`). The footer branch calls `read` on that child (line 62). With `tag === \"table\"` and `node !== owner`, line 32 returns `undefined`, and line 62 does `if (!span) return;` without a value. Line 65 then evaluates `implicitGroup && ... || tag === \"tr\" && ...` and passes; for an implicit `tbody`, `implicitGroup` is true, so line 69 evaluates `children.at(-1)!.span.end` on an empty array. `.at(-1)` is `undefined`, and `!` removes the type-only undefined check, so this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. The owner, whose own row count is below its first row, returns nothing. Nothing in `createSourceBusinessEvidenceCheck` catches the error (lines 142-164), so the caller never receives the `unknown` result the contract relies on. This contradicts the Cycle25 criterion that malformed tables must stay `unknown`. Whether `` is legal inside `` does not matter, because parse5's table insertion modes accept it. This finding does not depend on that parse outcome: the empty-`children` path is unreachable by inspection and is a guard bug in the current helper.","reproduction":"UNEXECUTED trace: save `x.html` containing `
TeaAUD18
xAUD 1
` and run `createSourceBusinessEvidenceCheck({\"x.html\":html}, [{checkId:\"c1\", criterionId:\"k\", file:\"x.html\", expected:{kind:\"price\", label:\"x\", currency:\"AUD\", amountMinor:100}}])(\"k\")`. `sourceFor` calls `tablePriceLeaves` for the second table, whose implicit `tbody` contains the nested table. The nested-table node fails line 32, `read` returns undefined at line 62, the `children` list stays empty, and line 69 throws. Fix line 62 to `if (!span) return undefined;` and add a test asserting that the result is `kind:\"unknown\"` and, under the proposed Cycle25 helper, `unknown_merged_price_options_unconfirmed` is never produced for malformed markup.","suggestion":"Always return explicitly: `if (!span) return undefined;` (and make the same intent explicit in line 62's early returns). Add a malformed-nested-table fixture asserting an `unknown` result, not an exception."},{"severity":"P3","file":"lib/source-business-evidence.ts","line":184,"title":"The covered-citation witness has no length budget, so a genuine cover fails as `unknown`","evidence":"Line 184, `expected.end - expected.start !== expected.excerpt.length`, requires the whole `excerpt` to match the span length. The cited check span comes from the `p`/`li` path, which limits excerpts to 500 UTF-16 units (line 107), and from the table row path, which limits them to 500 (line 78). Lines 187-190 then require one model citation to cover that span (`citation.start <= expected.start && citation.end >= expected.end`) with matching excerpt content. The Cycle25 task sends the recognized context through `assessSourceBusinessCitationWitness` with an 'exact budget', but the witness applies no budget of its own. Any model citation longer than the source span (a window of surrounding rows, or a span over 500 units) hits the excerpt-length inequality and is reported as `target_source_span_not_cited`. The witness then becomes `unknown` (line 193), and `sourceBusinessCitationWitnessExplanation` says the citation is incomplete. A citation that does contain the exact span is mislabeled as a coverage gap. The row-span citation Cycle25 proposes is the exact span, so this matters once the branch feeds the witness.","reproduction":"UNEXECUTED reasoning: expected = {file:\"menu.html\", start:10, end:80, excerpt:<70 chars>}; citation = {file:\"menu.html\", start:2, end:120, excerpt:<118 chars>} containing the expected 70 chars at the right offset. Line 188 requires `118 === 70` and fails, and line 190 (the positional substring check that would succeed) is never reached. Because of `&&` short-circuiting, the result is `unknown` / `target_source_span_not_cited` even though the citation covers the span exactly.","suggestion":"When a citation is longer than the expected span, compare by slicing the citation excerpt at the expected span's offset and length (`citation.excerpt.slice(expected.start - citation.start, expected.start - citation.start + (expected.end - expected.start)) === expected.excerpt`) instead of requiring equal lengths. Keep a separate explicit budget if desired, and test a covering citation with a wider window."},{"severity":"P3","file":"lib/source-business-evidence.ts","line":111,"title":"Design risk: the table owner is only detected from the third row onward, so an attributed first row is never inspected","evidence":"Line 111 pushes descendants of a table node with `hidden: ... [\"table\",\"li\"].includes(node.tagName)`. A nested table is therefore treated as hidden, and line 98 skips it. The proposed rowspan helper must run at the same point as line 98's owner detection. If the table is reached while its parent is a table (a nested table, or one that parse5 foster-parents), the first two rows are never inspected. For the Cycle25 target table the owner is top-level, so this does not apply to it. The risk appears wherever a valid two-row rowspan table sits inside another table: it silently stays the generic `unknown` even though the helper would say the merged options are confirmed. The current code exhibits the same skip for all table contents, so this is a design note, not a current bug.","reproduction":"UNEXECUTED reasoning: `
CategoryPrice
TeaAUD18
AUD28
AUD1
`: the inner table is reached with `hidden === true` from line 111 (the outer toggles it at line 111) and is skipped at line 98. Nothing recognizes the inner table at all.","suggestion":"Decide explicitly whether nested two-row tables are in scope. If they are not, document that and test it as unchanged `unknown`. If they are, call the helper when entering the table node instead of only on `inside && !hidden` nodes, and keep the payer outer row as part of the owner window."},{"severity":"P3","file":"lib/source-business-evidence.ts","line":78,"title":"Design risk: the recognized merged-option evidence must stay out of priceLeaves, or the unchanged branch can read it as a single compound price","evidence":"Line 78 pushes a rowspan row (label `Tea`, value `AUD18`) as a normal leaf with `{label, text: label + \" \" + value, citation: }`. Line 157 matches leaves by `leaf.label === label` or `leaf.text.startsWith(label)`, trailing whitespace only. Under the proposed helper, a first row bound by `rowspan=\"2\"` is the only row that carries the label, so it becomes the sole match. Tail `\"AUD18\"` parses at line 159 and, if it equals the agreed amount, line 163 returns `unchanged` on the first row while the second row (`AUD28`, whose option is undetermined) is ignored. The canonical `unknown_merged_price_options_unconfirmed` branch would be bypassed. The second row alone fails line 65 (`children.length !== 2`) and is rejected, so the ambiguity is invisible to the price branch. The proposal itself must therefore route recognized contexts to the unknown branch before the price branch, and must not leak rowspan rows into `priceLeaves`.","reproduction":"UNEXECUTED reasoning: with the owner `Tea/rowspan=2 → AUD18`, `AUD28`, expected label `Tea` and `AUD 18.00`, if the first row is in `priceLeaves`, then `occurrences(bodyText,\"Tea\")` (line 156) is 1 because only one row contains the label, `matching.length` is 1 at line 158, the tail parses at line 159, and line 163 returns `kind:\"unchanged\"`. The buyer would see a pass even though the order's applicable amount is unresolved.","suggestion":"Recognize the two-row owner before the label/price branch and return `unknown_merged_price_options_unconfirmed` with both amounts. Never add rowspan rows to `priceLeaves`. Add a test asserting that the merged table yields `unknown` with both amounts and never `unchanged` or `mismatch`."}]}
